summary: LeafWiki is a lightweight wiki engine that organises documentation in a hierarchical tree structure using standard Markdown files stored directly on disk. It provides fast editing capabilities and relies on folder-based navigation rather than chronological feeds.
goodFor: It is a strong fit if you prefer maintaining your documentation repository as plain files on a local filesystem while retaining a web-based interface for reading and editing.
watchOut: As a relatively niche project with a modest community compared to mainstream alternatives, you may need to handle custom integrations and extensions yourself.
deployNotes: Because the application is packaged as a Docker container using Go, you will typically need to configure persistent volume storage for your Markdown files and place it behind a reverse proxy for TLS termination.
